# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F |
| Logged-in domain user | ccollier (domain: wiresharkworkshop.online, DC: WIRESHARK-WS-DC) |
| OS (self-reported in C2 beacon) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit |

Confirmed via NBNS name registrations (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F`), Kerberos CNameString (`ccollier`, `desktop-skbr25f$`), and the malware's own telemetry beacon (below), all pointing to the same host/user.

## 2. Malware Family

**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/backdoor).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The malware's own cleartext C2 beacon contains the literal string `STRRAT` as a protocol field, plus a hardware ID, hostname, username, OS info, AV product, and active window title — this is STRRAT's well-known pipe-delimited "ping" telemetry format. This is not inferred from behavior alone; the malware self-identifies in the traffic.

Example beacon (TCP stream 83, frame ~9119 onward):
```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|5 min 10 sec
```
(`UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy` base64-decodes to `Program Manager`, the active foreground window — a known STRRAT field.)

Supporting behavioral evidence consistent with STRRAT (a JAR-based RAT that runs under the Java runtime): DNS lookups to `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` (Java runtime check-in), and downloads from `github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com`, and `repo1.maven.org` (Java dependency/library retrieval) immediately preceding C2 activation.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command and Control
- **C2 endpoint: 141.98.10.79:12132** (plaintext TCP, no TLS)
- First contact: t+76.99s (SYN); beaconing every ~5 seconds continuously through the end of the capture (t+585.66s, ~8.5 minutes of sustained C2 traffic on TCP stream 83)
- Malware/campaign ID embedded in beacon: `1BE8292C`

### Supporting/staging infrastructure observed in traffic
- `github.com` (140.82.113.3) — TLS, first DNS lookup at t+63.96s
- `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133) — TLS, t+64.77s
- `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209) — TLS, large burst (~8.8 MB in 5.8s at t+64.83s–70.66s), consistent with Java dependency/JAR retrieval
- `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` (23.194.164.136) — TLS, Java update/runtime probe

Note: all of the above are legitimate-service domains (GitHub, Maven Central, Oracle) used as delivery/staging infrastructure and carried over TLS, so specific file names/paths and hashes could not be extracted from this capture — no plaintext HTTP transfer of a payload file was observed.

### Reconnaissance / victim profiling
- **ip-api.com (208.95.112.1), plaintext HTTP GET /json/** at t+78.01s — classic malware victim-geolocation lookup, occurring seconds after the first C2 SYN. User-Agent spoofed as `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ... Chrome/73.0.3683.86`. Response confirmed geolocation returned to the beacon field `US:United States`.

### Malicious domains (DNS resolved by victim)
- None of the resolved domains are themselves attacker-registered/typosquat domains — all C2 traffic used a raw IP (141.98.10.79), not a domain name. No malicious URL or dropped file could be recovered from the capture (all relevant transfers were TLS-encrypted; no file names or SHA256 hashes are present in the traffic).

## 4. Summary

172.16.1.66 (DESKTOP-SKBR25F, user ccollier) is actively compromised with STRRAT. Around t+64s the host pulled Java components from GitHub/GitHub-objects/Maven Central, then at t+77s began sustained cleartext C2 beaconing to 141.98.10.79:12132, self-identifying as STRRAT with hardware ID 1BE8292C, immediately followed by a victim-IP geolocation lookup to ip-api.com. Beaconing continued uninterrupted for the remainder of the capture (~8.5 minutes), indicating an active, unremediated infection at capture end.

**Recommended immediate action:** isolate 172.16.1.66 from the network, block egress to 141.98.10.79:12132, force credential reset for ccollier and any accounts used on that host, and hunt for STRRAT JAR artifacts and persistence (STRRAT commonly persists via a Startup-folder or registry Run-key entry launching `javaw.exe`).
